analysis.title: NVIDIA: Few Options - None of Them Good
key_insights: Seaport says the NVDA Board faces two bad options: replace CEO Jensen Huang and incur a rough transition (possibly via an interim leader), or keep him and weather a long period of controversy.
Per the note, press reports say the Board met the night before to remove Huang after further allegations of personal misconduct. Seaport would view his removal as a mistake.

If Huang stays, Seaport expects continued scrutiny: NVDA is already under multiple government investigations, Congress is likely to get involved, and management will be distracted for months. The order book stretching into next year would support the business, and Seaport has heard no sign that customers are moving away from orders.

If Huang is removed, Seaport expects a sharp drop in the stock (indicated down 9% after hours as of writing) and a period of uncertainty until a new CEO is named. It argues no successor matches his force of personality across the industry.

Seaport says NVDA's siloed structure leaves Huang deeply involved in all major decisions, so an internal candidate would be expert in one area but unaware of large parts of the business. A full reorganization around a new leader would take many quarters.
Seaport expects a successor to run a competent but less dynamic company while NVDA faces growing competition, further restrictions on sales to Asia and rising capital demands from customers.

Near-term AI spending is seen as largely unchanged because 2027 contracts are largely signed and difficult to cancel. Seaport expects AI spending to continue through next year, with 2028 becoming tougher as the industry loses its chief booster.

Seaport expects pressure on neoclouds. It thinks Huang's proposed $500B financing platform would likely be abandoned without him. The six private equity funds named in the press release two months ago have still not finalized their contract.
Seaport says NVDA's distraction gives hyperscalers and AI labs more reason to diversify chip sourcing, calling bad news at NVDA good news for AMD and Broadcom.

Seaport sees a mixed picture for neoclouds. CoreWeave indicated on its call that it is moving away from reliance on NVDA backstops, which Seaport says would be moderately good news if achieved but is by no means certain.
Seaport notes an Anthropic IPO is likely next week and, given press reports that it is oversubscribed, could be a positive catalyst for AI generally.

Seaport's Sell rating and $180 price target (DCF, 6.5% growth rate, 11% discount rate) are under review pending clarity on the company's situation. The stock was at $173.73, so the target sits about 3.6% above the current price.

market_movers.rationale: Rating and $180 target are under review pending clarity on the CEO situation. The target is based on a DCF with 6.5% growth and an 11% discount rate. The stock was at $173.73.
Seaport says bad news at NVDA is good news for AMD, as hyperscalers and AI labs have more motivation to diversify semiconductor sourcing.
Seaport says bad news at NVDA is good news for Broadcom, as hyperscalers and AI labs have more motivation to diversify semiconductor sourcing.

Seaport sees a mixed picture for CoreWeave. Moving away from NVDA backstops, as indicated on its call, would be moderately good news if achieved. Without the financing platform it risks less NVDA support.

sector_views.rationale: Seaport expects AI spending to continue through next year on largely signed 2027 contracts. It sees 2028 as tougher without Huang as the industry's chief booster, and expects share diversification toward AMD and Broadcom.

earnings_insights: Seaport's NVDA estimates are under review. Its FY (Jan) revenue estimates: FY2026 $215,938MM actual, FY2027 $410,429MM estimate, FY2028 $675,095MM estimate.
Seaport's adjusted EPS: FY2026 $5.18 actual, FY2027 $9.32 estimate, FY2028 $15.09 estimate. Quarterly estimates: Q3 (Oct) 2027 $2.56E and Q4 (Jan) $2.67E, with revenue of $112,499MM and $120,094MM.
At the $173.73 price, Seaport's table shows P/E of 33.5x on 2026 actual, 18.6x on 2027 estimates and 11.5x on 2028 estimates. EV/Sales is 19.4x, 10.2x and 6.2x.
risk_factors: CEO removal triggering a sharp stock drop and a leadership vacuum until a new CEO is named.
Prolonged controversy, government investigations and a likely congressional inquiry if Huang stays, with management distracted for months.
Abandonment of the $500B neocloud financing platform without Huang, pressuring neoclouds that depend on NVDA support.
Growing competition, further restrictions on sales to Asia and mounting customer demand for capital.
A tougher AI spending environment in 2028 as the industry loses its chief booster.

Seaport lists short interest of 279.6MM shares against a float of 23,190.4MM, and average daily volume of 140,114k. The 52-week range is $164.27 to $243.37.

tension_points.bull_case: If Huang stays, NVDA keeps its leading industry position, supported by a strong order book stretching into next year and no sign that customers are moving away from orders.
tension_points.bear_case: If Huang stays, management faces months of government investigations, a likely congressional inquiry and years of rebuilding credibility. If he is removed, Seaport expects a sharp stock drop and quarters of reorganization, ending in a competent but less dynamic company.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Seaport's read that customers are not moving away from orders would be invalidated by signs of order cancellations or diversification beyond what it has heard.
